questions.prompt: `claude --version` prints a version number, but when you ask Claude Code to read README.md it cannot. What is going on, and what do you do?
options: The install succeeded — the version printed, so start working

Presence is not correctness: a shim is imitating the tool well enough to pass a version check. Verify by asking it to read a named file and report a true fact; if it cannot, reinstall from the official source
The file must not exist — check the path
The model is offline — wait and retry
questions.explanation: The install command printing a number only proves something is on PATH, not that the real tool works. Option A is the trap the lesson exists to break: it trusts presence over use. Option C blames the fixture when the real signal is that reading a file you named is the check a shim cannot pass. Option D guesses at a cause the evidence does not support.

questions.prompt: Your Phase 00 setup-check reports `claude: shim`. What does that mean?
options: The binary is missing from PATH entirely
A file named claude is on PATH and imitates the tool well enough to fool a presence check, but is not the real tool
The installed version is out of date
questions.explanation: A shim is a stand-in that passes a presence check, which is exactly why the script distinguishes it from a real binary. Option A is the tempting confusion: `MISS` means absent; `shim` means present and imitating. Option C confuses an out-of-date install with a fake one. Option D blames the messenger instead of the report it carries.

questions.prompt: Which check actually proves a Claude Code install is real rather than a shim?
options: Ask it to read a file you named and report a fact that matches the file's contents
The tool launches and shows a prompt
questions.explanation: Reading a file you named and reporting a true fact is a task a shim cannot fake, which is what makes it verification. Options A, B, and D are all presence checks: a version string, a PATH hit, and a prompt on screen can each be produced by something that is not the real tool. Option B is the most tempting of the three because it looks like a real lookup, but a lookup is still not correctness.

questions.prompt: A blog post gives a one-line install command for Claude Code that differs from the official docs page. What do you do?
options: Run the blog command — one-liners are usually the same
Use the official command for your platform from the docs; do not improvise
Run both and keep whichever prints a version
Skip the install and use the browser version instead
questions.explanation: The install command is one line and you take it from the official source, because a third-party variant is how you end up with an old binary or, worse, a shim. Option A is tempting because the difference usually looks cosmetic. Option C decides by a presence check, which is the exact test the lesson says is not enough. Option D abandons the terminal shape the whole phase is about.
